question: The Commission has highlighted water resilience as a European priority, emphasising the need to protect the water cycle, reduce leakages, modernise infrastructure and improve water efficiency. In parallel, a specific technical support project was approved for 2026 to modernise the management of water services in Greece. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How will it monitor whether Greece is using EU technical support to achieve genuine water management reform and not to make purely formal administrative changes?
Does it intend to ask the Greek Government for quantitative targets for leakage reduction, water reuse, groundwater protection and support for rural areas affected by drought?
Will it link future water funding to measurable results and transparency in the way water providers operate?
answer: The Commission will monitor EU technical support to Greece through standard Technical Support Instrument governance (1), including the Log Frame Approach with outcome/impact indicators. Greece remains subject to EU water acquis obligations. The Commission will follow implementation closely with Greek authorities and partners to ensure operational, not merely administrative, improvements.

The aim is to strengthen the governance, functioning and efficiency of water services. Under the recast Drinking Water Directive (2), Member States reported leakage assessments by January 2026; the Commission will propose a leakage threshold via delegated act by January 2028. The Water Reuse Regulation (3) sets no mandatory targets and will be evaluated by June 2028.

The Water Framework Directive (4) requires good quantitative groundwater status by 2027. Under the Water Resilience Strategy (5), guidance on drought management and drought indicators will be published in 2026. Under the Cohesion Policy 2021-2027 (6), water sector performance is monitored via output/result indicators, with reimbursement conditional on the applicable thematic enabling condition (7).
The next Multiannual Financial Framework (8) proposal includes water investment fields, with a performance framework for transparent monitoring of EU financial support.
